items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: That's the first time High Society had been made since Joe Oliver made it.

ctx.x: Yes. Because the, uh, the guy wanted to know, you know, who, who, who, who, who's the composer of the tune. So I thought, I said, well, I don't know. That's the first time High Society had been made since Joe Oliver made it. He said, Joe Oliver made it first. Well, nobody knew who it belonged to, you know. It's just like, like, like Tiger Egg and, and the, and the other ones. Uh, so he said, well, we'll put your name on it. Uh, so he did, he put my name down as a composer. And then, then before the record came…

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: I seen him in California... Old Man King kept telling him to quit playing those high notes... they run Rap out of the studio

ctx.x: Who made the records? Do you know?

Yeah. The ones they made here, you mean? Uh, uh... August Schillang on drums. Uh... Santo, Rap. Well now they made... They made two sessions here. They made an OK session here and they made a Victor session here. The OK was with Santo, Rap, Paul... Steve Loiskaner, Freddie Newman, piano, and Chink. And a tenor? Lester. Lester Bouchon. Yeah. And the drums? August Schillang. Yeah. The Victor date, it started out with the same band, but Rap, Old Man King was the recording you used. You ought to know about him…
The others were all the same? They only made... I mean the others were all the same, the drummer and all. Yeah. No, no, no, with the...
